Hermes blocks the agent thread on an in-memory threading.Event with a deadline, and replays open requests only to reconnecting clients while the process lives. Present durable approval pauses as a Verevon design synthesis (INF) built from DeepSeek checkpoints, not as a reference behavior. 2) The Manus 'exactly-once ledger' is a process-local, in-memory Map (max 4096 entries, 10-minute horizon) scoped to browser MCP side-effect actions only. Mismatched digests return a replay-conflict result (confirmed). 3) DeepSeek explicitly disclaims exactly-once: it records dispatch intent, writes an unknown-outcome closer instead of retrying, and recommends forwarding exec.callId as an idempotency key. It has no checkpoint inside an active model attempt. 4) Cursor auto-continue and durable question delivery are server-flag-gated (glass_auto_continue_*, ask_question_durable_delivery fallback default off). 5) Hermes failover reasons: 29, so 'about 30' is fine.
